subject: Follow up Remarks on Budget Funds Regarding Nevada St CIP Application
comment: Hello Council Members, I hope you all had a nice holiday weekend. I was signed up to make comments at the meeting last week and had to cancel last minute with a personal matter. It took me through the weekend and I am just now able to follow up. Below are my 2min worth of remarks I would have made last week. Thank you for your time in reading them. Sincerely, Nick Wilkinson Hello Council Members. Thank you for your time. I first want to say that as someone who has submitted multiple CIP applications and helped coach others on how to submit CIP applications, it is a bit disheartening to see that out of 92 applications, 24 were recommended for funding. And out of those 24, only 2 were constituent applications. I am here to highlight the Nevada Street Rebuild CIP application. This CIP reaches farther than just Nevada St. It will have a positive impact with a focus on safety, for so much of the east bench as so many families use this street for school pick up and drop off as well as after school and weekend activities. My name is Nicholas Wilkinson and I am a Trustee for the Beacon Heights neighborhood as part of the Sugar House Community Council. In being one of the trustees for this neighborhood since 2020, I have heard a lot about Nevada St... It is a direct thoroughfare for two schools and is in a neighborhood of four total schools. (Hillside Middle School, Coygrill Elementary, Beacon Heights Elementary, and Foothill Montessori of Salt Lake). There have been an increasing number of safety concerns brought up with the street and to the Mayor's office, the School District, and school Principles through the years. As a background, Nevada St. has been on the list of streets that need work since 2018. Now currently sitting at an OCI overall condition index in the low teens (13). The reason I titled this CIP "Nevada St. Rebuild" is that, that is the first thing that needs to happen to properly implement the safety improvement. ADA compliant ramps, painted crosswalks, coordinated updated signage, and updated curbs for drainage as there is standing water. All of these need the street to be fixed first as they would just deteriorate along with it if the street was not completed initially. Thank you for listening to a brief overview of the project and considering this as you move forward with budget discussions. -- Nick Wilkinson

subject: Rate increase for waste and recycling
comment: Dear City Council, I received notice of the proposed increase in both the garbage fee and the recycling fee. I am more than satisfied by how these services are delivered, and I totally understand the need for increased revenue to fund them. That said, people like myself are sharing more than our share of the burden. I am a widowed senior, living alone with a very modest lifestyle. I subscribe to the smallest available garbage container (40 gallons) that I have collected once EVERY 6-8 WEEKS (and it is never full); my recycling bin is put out never more than 1x/month; I compost nearly all my kitchen and yard waste so the "brown bin" is only used in the fall when I collect leaves from the street (the city's responsibility, but you're a bit slow) that I don't want to put on my vegetable gardens. Modern technology should easily allow you to know how often (and how much) my waste is collected. Can't I be billed accordingly? The only incentive we have to contribute less waste to the system is the tiered rate of the garbage containers and that rate favors the largest users-- they get 2.25 more capacity for 0.5 more cost. Water rates increase with usage....why not waste? You need more customers like me...give us a few perks, thanks, Kirk Kirk Thomas

subject: Rate structure
comment: The structure shown as an explanation of the new rates does not do enough to encourage conservation. The difference between block rates reduces as more water is used. The opposite block rate graduation should be in effect. The difference between blocks should increase as they go up. Those using more water should be paying a much higher rate. Perhaps there should even be more steps in the block system. I appreciate getting rid of some of the fees, but I still feel that water usage charge is hidden as a very small portion of the bill. Billing should do more to encourage less water use.

subject: Bryan Ave Road Condition
comment: Dear Salt Lake City Officials, I am writing as a homeowner and longtime resident of REDACTED to respectfully bring to your attention the urgent and worsening condition of our street. While neighboring roads have been resurfaced—some even multiple times—over the past few years, our block continues to deteriorate with no clear timeline for repair. Currently, the pavement on our street holds a condition rating of just 16 out of 100, which speaks for itself. The road surface is so broken and uneven that children in our neighborhood are unable to safely ride their bikes or scooters without risk of injury. The gutters are no longer functioning properly and regularly collect stagnant water, creating a breeding ground for mosquitoes and posing a potential health concern. This issue impacts not just our immediate neighbors but the broader community as well. Our street serves as a high-traffic route for both vehicles and students commuting to and from Clayton Middle School, located just around the corner. With the volume of kids walking, biking, and being dropped off daily, the condition of our street is a serious safety concern. We are proud residents who care deeply about the condition and livability of our neighborhood. It's disheartening to see surrounding streets prioritized while ours—despite being in far worse condition—is left behind. We would greatly appreciate a response outlining any upcoming plans for reconstruction or repair, and we hope the city will recognize the importance of addressing this issue promptly. Thank you for your time, attention, and commitment to keeping our neighborhoods safe, accessible, and well-maintained. Sincerely, Teryn Holeman & Alex Huth Homeowner

subject: Warm Springs
comment: Reviewing the District 3 Newsletter recently, I noticed the comments on improving our parks, currently focussing on Lindsay Gardens. I also noticed a comment about planning improvements for Warm Springs. Clearly the improvements and completion of the restoration of Warm Springs is well over due. I appreciate the stabilization work that has been done to protect the building and the fact that Chris has pushed the funding forward for this work. However, the potential of Warm Springs is being ignored or avoided for some reason. Is this lack of progress a City or a State problem? Warm Springs is an opportunity to connect East and West SLC as it did for many years. It also has a significant Native American connection that should be shared daily with those who will visit and utilize Warm Springs. At this point it is a resource with no clear direction. I suggest it is time for SLC to actively lead the efforts to restore Warm Springs for the benefit of SLC residents and visitors. Regards, Peter Emerson
